stories.title: Central bank raises policy rate by 50 basis points to 12pc
summary: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) on Monday raised the key policy rate by 50 basis points to 12 per cent, its first increase since April as inflation, fuelled by high energy costs due to the Gulf conflict, remained above target.

The inflation outlook is subject to multiple risks, including geopolitical tensions, global commodity price volatility, unanticipated adjustments in energy tariffs, further uptick in wheat and allied product prices and adverse weather conditions,” it said.
The central bank had held the rate steady since raising it by 100 basis points in April in response to rising global energy prices and supply chain risks — its first increase in nearly three years.

stories.title: Jordan arrests 3 in dawn raid over church attack
summary: Jordanian security forces on Monday arrested three suspects over an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, with the trio wounded in a dawn raid and shootout, authorities said.
Earlier, the king visited the injured victims of the church attack in hospital, dressed in military fatigues and carrying a pistol on his hip. “We will show them,” he vowed.

On Friday, Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning for the victims of the church attack, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.

stories.title: Pakistan, China call for enhanced cooperation between foreign ministries: FO
summary: During the third round of the Pakistan-China Spokespersons’ Dialogue in Islamabad on Monday, the two countries called for bolstered cooperation between their foreign ministries as well as in the areas of media engagement and strategic communication, the Foreign Office (FO) said.
Dar also stressed the importance of enhanced media cooperation, strategic communication and public diplomacy to advance bilateral relations and foster closer people-to-people ties.
Pakistan and China share a longstanding strategic partnership rooted in mutual trust, economic cooperation and regional connectivity.

stories.title: Encounter culture

stories.title: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations
summary: The Afghan Taliban have repeatedly claimed civilian casualties in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan; Pakistani authorities have denied the accusations, holding that they target military and terrorist infrastructure.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan.

It also rebutted the Afghan Taliban’s stance that it lacked the “capabilities” to fuel insecurity in other countries and criticised it for resorting to “diversionary allegations” instead of preventing the use of Afghanistan’s soil for terrorist attacks against Pakistan.

stories.title: Former army chief Abdul Waheed Kakar passes away in Rawalpindi
summary: Former army chief Abdul Waheed Kakar passed away in Rawalpindi on Monday, a statement by the military’s media affairs wing said.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, expressing condolences at the death of the former general, paid tribute to his “invaluable services” to the Pakistan Armed Forces, state broadcaster PTV reported.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, in a post on X, said he was “deeply saddened” by Kakar’s passing. “His distinguished service to Pakistan and the Pakistan Army will be remembered with the highest regard,” Dar wrote, praying for the deceased’s family.

stories.title: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks targeting Makkah, Madina as 'grave violation' of Saudi sovereignty
summary: Pakistan on Monday condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s Makkah and Madina regions, terming them a “grave violation” of the kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Saudi Civil Defence said debris from intercepted missiles had fallen in the Makkah and Madina regions.
The Houthis subsequently denied targeting Makkah and Madina, saying their operations were directed at “Saudi oil facilities and military bases”.

stories.title: Netanyahu denies reports of clash with Israeli army chief over Iran-linked operation ahead of election
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday denied reports of a clash with Army Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir over a proposed military operation that could trigger fighting with Iran ahead of Israel’s election.
Netanyahu denied any dispute with Zamir during an interview with Israel’s Channel 14 later on Sunday. “There is no confrontation,” he said.
We absolutely must send him home.” Netanyahu also claimed Iran had resumed its nuclear programme and portrayed the election as a matter of Israel’s survival.

stories.title: What challenges await Brazil's Lula in his fourth term?
summary: President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva will have to wrestle with a divided Brazil, an unfriendly Congress, feeble public finances and a Donald Trump-shaped menace during his unprecedented fourth term.

summary: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye will travel to Tehran on Monday, according to an Iranian and a Saudi official.

stories.title: JI threatens march to Islamabad in mid-November if petroleum levy not abolished
summary: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Monday warned that the party would march to Islamabad in mid-November if Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif did not abolish the petroleum levy.

Rehman said his party remained prepared to march towards Islamabad and recalled that federal ministers had contacted the party repeatedly. “Liaquat Baloch Sahib has told them that nothing will come out of talks until something tangible is given,” he said.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: India to evacuate thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears eastern coast
summary: Two states along India’s eastern coast were preparing to evacuate thousands of people ahead of Cyclone ​Arnab, which is expected to make landfall ‌on Wednesday, as one of them said it would close schools in some districts for two days.

Arnab, which formed over ​the Bay of Bengal before intensifying into ​a cyclonic storm, is expected to make landfall ⁠in Andhra Pradesh state by Wednesday morning, with gusts of ​as much as 140 kph (87 mph), India’s weather office ​said.
The weather system is expected to bring heavy to extremely heavy rainfall to Andhra ​Pradesh’s northern and central coastal districts, and southern ​regions of neighbouring Odisha.

stories.title: Shadab Khan's maiden ODI century steers Pakistan into tri-series final after thrilling chase against England
summary: With the last wicket standing and Haris Rauf holding firm at the other end, Pakistan needed 27 runs when Shadab swept Gus Atkinson for six over fine leg.

stories.title: #Watch #Chaudhry #Solar #foryou: Hotwiring rural Punjab
summary: Spending several months across the rural countryside in Punjab, Zainaab spotted solar panels propped up on bamboo sticks, lying down amidst wheatfields, and spoke to people who brought them there.
But two other findings stand out: the demonstration effect of rich landlords installing solar on their land and the ease with which such panels can be installed using social media.

Solar adoption by landlords had a powerful demonstration effect on surrounding poorer communities, who were now exposed to a purportedly transformative technology at the very moment they needed an off-ramp from grid and diesel-based electricity.

stories.title: Saim Ayub released from Pakistan tri-series squad to work on batting form, Sahibzada Farhan named replacement
summary: Pakistan opener Saim Ayub has been released from the national squad for the remainder of the ongoing One-day International tri-series after requesting to return to domestic cricket to work on his batting form and regain confidence, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) said on Monday.

stories.title: Officials from Makkah pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran
summary: Top officials from Makkah Pact countries ​Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are to meet Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday in their first high-level contact since the kingdom became a pressure point in ‌the wider Iran conflict.

Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Turkiye by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said.
A senior Iranian official said the meeting was initiated by Pakistan during CDF Munir's visit to Tehran, as he met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and other senior officials.

stories.title: Australia eye Renshaw for final Test
summary: Australia are considering a change at the top of their batting order for the decisive third Test against South Africa, with Matthew Renshaw in contention to partner Travis Head after Nic Maddinson struggled in the opening two matches of the series.

The potential change follows Australia's batting difficulties in the second Test at Gqeberha, where South Africa responded emphatically to their defeat in the series opener by securing an innings and 31-run victory.
Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs before South Africa levelled the series with their commanding performance in Gqeberha.

stories.title: Brazil's leftist President Lula wins fourth term in dramatic comeback
summary: Brazil’s leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva pulled off a dramatic comeback on Sunday as he clinched a re-election victory, but his rival Flavio Bolsonaro refused to accept the loss and said he would seek to annul the vote.
With Lula’s victory, Brazil staved off a conservative wave that has seen numerous countries — such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru — all shift right, backed by US President Donald Trump.
The senator is the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year jail term for attempting a coup after his loss to Lula in the country’s last election in 2022.

Chairing a meeting of the Punjab Saaf Pani Authority, the chief minister assigned the responsibility of monitoring water filtration plants to the respective assistant commissioners.
Each mobile workshop will have plumbers and other technical staff to ensure timely maintenance of the plants and people’s uninterrupted access to clean drinking water.

stories.title: Experts call for preventive measures as dengue cases continue to rise in KP
summary: PESHAWAR: The cases of dengue fever continued to rise in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa during October, the peak month for infection, with the provincial tally reaching 4,856 after 51 new cases were reported on Sunday.

The latest dengue situation report, released by Integrated Diseases Surveillance and Response System (IDSRS) at Directorate General Health Services of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, shows that 2,244 cases have been reported during the current month.
Health officials said that October had traditionally been the most infectious period of the year as the highest number of dengue cases were reported during that month.

stories.title: Israel extends military barrier through farmland in southern Syria
summary: Israeli forces continued bulldozing farmland in southern Syria on Sunday to extend a military barrier that Damascus has condemned as a violation of the 1974 disengagement agreement, the official SANA news agency reported.

Israeli forces carried out a similar incursion near Jubata al-Khashab on Saturday, according to the agency.
